children: Historical patterns in U.S. midterm election years show a pronounced late-year lift for equities. Analysis of S&P 500 (
) monthly returns from 1950 through 2025, compiled by Carson Group, finds October to be the strongest month on average.
October advances typically land with a 3.0% gain and positive results in 73.7% of those years. November ranks second, advancing 2.7% on average and finishing higher 78.9% of the time.

The contrast with earlier months is sharp. June has been the weakest, averaging a 2.1% decline and rising in only 36.8% of midterm years. September also tends to lag, with an average 0.8% drop and gains in just 47.4% of observations. January and May have likewise posted modest average losses. March and July have delivered smaller but positive averages, while December has typically added 0.8%.

With the next midterm cycle approaching, those late-year tendencies are drawing attention. Ryan Detrick of Carson Group has highlighted October’s and November’s standout records. The data does not guarantee any outcome in the current cycle, yet they help explain why some market participants watch for positioning as the calendar turns from September into the historically stronger window.
Seasonality is only one input among valuations, policy, and growth, but the long-run midterm-year pattern remains a frequently cited reference for investors tracking the political calendar.

title: Midterm playbook: History favors a late-year lift in October and November
